page_scale.scale_method: One isotropic scale from 13 common capital width/height pairs. Transfer to figure page using repeated header width ratio; no figure height normalization and no row-specific scale.
page_scale.header_transfer_method: 47 matched glyph centers at threshold 130; five-threshold stability check. One scale for both figure-font rows.

header_scale_transfer.method: One isotropic similarity transform from 47 corresponding running-header glyph centers. Letter boundaries mapped at threshold 150 and measured at five thresholds.
header_scale_transfer.visual_review: The retained full running headers have matching construction, wording and spacing. No figure dimensions enter this scale transfer.
header_scale_transfer.threshold_stability: Thresholds 110–170 give 0.46–0.58 native-pixel RMS and scales 1.000874–1.001214. Threshold 90 loses part of a faint glyph and has an 11.85-pixel outlier; it is not used. Selected threshold 130 gives scale 1.00116754, RMS 0.502, maximum 0.903.

common_capital_comparison.method: Repeated header line width calibrates each new page to the existing regular Job84 source scale. This is independent of the provisional poster-cap normalization.
common_capital_comparison.status: Native and outline comparisons reviewed; adopt one corrected isotropic page scale from thirteen common capitals.

caps.method: Measured row baseline and rigid rotation; one fixed physical scale per page from common capitals and matched header centers.

poster-figures.method: Measured row baseline and rigid rotation; one fixed physical scale per page from common capitals and matched header centers.

close-figures.method: Measured row baseline and rigid rotation; one fixed physical scale per page from common capitals and matched header centers.

spaced-figures.method: Measured row baseline and rigid rotation; one fixed physical scale per page from common capitals and matched header centers.

body-00.method: Theil-Sen slope and median intercept of six distributed flat-bottom lowercase letters, threshold 150.

identity_limit: Optical correspondence and consistent scale support the revival grouping; they do not establish identical physical punches or matrices.

reused_figure_comparison.status: Reviewed at fixed page scale: reuse existing three,four,six,eight; no duplicate alternate glyphs.
reused_figure_comparison.decision: Whole forms correspond optically, including counters and terminals. Existing higher-resolution Census traces retain sharper six tail and native source positions. Small 1–2% height/baseline differences between impressions do not justify duplicate forms or moving encoded figures.
